title: Listed company exposure to government budget lines, Kenya
basis: Each entry states a mechanical link between a sector ceiling in static_data/gov_budget_KE.json and a company that exists in static_data/listing_NSE.json. The link is a channel, not a forecast. Nothing here says a company will earn more or less, nothing here is a recommendation, and no entry is a valuation input. A company appears only where the channel can be described in one factual sentence from what the company does and what the budget line funds.

directness_definitions.direct: The company's own product or service is paid for with money from this ceiling, or the company holds contracts that this ceiling pays for. The channel runs from the allocation to the company's revenue in one step.
directness_definitions.indirect: The channel runs through at least one intermediate party or through costs and demand rather than through a purchase order. The company's revenue does not appear on the face of the budget line.

indirect.reason: Sasini is a listed grower and processor of tea, coffee and other crops; the ARUD ceiling funds the input subsidy, extension and irrigation programmes that set the cost and yield environment for those crops.
Kakuzi grows tea, avocados and macadamia; the same ARUD programmes fund input support and extension for crop growers.
Williamson Tea is a tea grower; the ARUD ceiling funds the agricultural input and extension programmes that apply to tea.
Limuru Tea is a tea grower; the ARUD ceiling funds the agricultural input and extension programmes that apply to tea.
Kapchorua Tea is a tea grower; the ARUD ceiling funds the agricultural input and extension programmes that apply to tea.
Eaagads grows coffee; the ARUD ceiling funds the crop input and extension programmes that apply to coffee.
Unga Group mills wheat and maize; the ARUD ceiling funds the grain and fertiliser programmes that shape its raw material supply and cost.
Africa Mega Agricorp is a large scale farming company; the ARUD ceiling funds the input, irrigation and extension programmes aimed at large and small scale farming.

Agriculture, Rural and Urban Development.no_direct_supplier_reason: No company in the NSE listing sells goods or services that are paid for directly from this ceiling. The land, survey and title functions inside ARUD have no listed supplier.

direct.reason: Bamburi Cement sells cement; the EII ceiling funds the road and housing programmes whose contractors purchase cement.
East African Portland Cement sells cement; the EII ceiling funds the road and housing programmes whose contractors purchase it.
Crown Paints sells paints and coatings; the EII ceiling funds the housing and public building programmes whose contractors purchase them.
Flame Tree Group makes building products; the EII ceiling funds the housing and public building programmes that consume them.
East African Cables makes power and construction cables; the EII ceiling funds the transmission, distribution and electrification works that consume cable.
Trans-Century is an engineering and infrastructure contractor; the EII ceiling funds the road, power and building contracts it bids for.

indirect.reason: BOC Kenya supplies industrial gases used in fabrication and construction; the EII ceiling funds the works that consume them.
Sameer Africa sells tyres and automotive products; the EII ceiling funds the road programme that generates the vehicle traffic those products serve.
Express Kenya is a logistics and warehousing operator; the EII ceiling funds the transport infrastructure it moves goods over.
Kenya Airways earns passenger and cargo revenue; the EII ceiling funds the aviation and airport infrastructure it operates from, but its revenue is ticket revenue, not a budget line.
TPS Eastern Africa (Serena) operates hotels; the GECA ceiling funds the tourism marketing and destination promotion programmes that shape arrival numbers.

General Economic and Commercial Affairs.no_direct_supplier_reason: No NSE listed company sells directly into the trade, industry, standards or MSME programmes in this ceiling.

Health.no_direct_supplier_reason: No company in the NSE listing has a revenue line that is paid from the health vote in a way that can be stated mechanically from a primary document inside this task. Hospital construction is funded across several votes, and the construction material suppliers are recorded once, under EII, rather than counted twice here.

direct.reason: Longhorn Publishers publishes approved school textbooks and revision material; the education ceiling funds the school capitation and instructional material budgets that purchase them.

Governance, Justice, Law and Order (GJLO.no_direct_supplier_reason: The suppliers to the police, prison and court votes are not identifiable from the NSE listing. Security and correctional equipment suppliers that do exist are not listed in Nairobi.

Public Administration and International.no_direct_supplier_reason: This ceiling funds ministries and diplomatic missions, not procurement of a listed company's output. Public debt service, which is the largest single charge on the budget, sits outside the sector ceilings and is handled in the cross_cutting block.

National Security.no_direct_supplier_reason: Defence procurement in Kenya is not channelled through NSE listed suppliers.

Social Protection, Culture and Recreatio.no_direct_supplier_reason: The largest line here is cash transfers to individuals, which reach households rather than companies.

direct.reason: Bamburi Cement sells cement; the EPWNR ceiling funds the dam, water and irrigation works whose contractors purchase cement.
East African Portland Cement sells cement; the EPWNR ceiling funds the dam, water and irrigation works whose contractors purchase it.

cross_cutting.label: Government borrowing and the banking sector
cross_cutting.note: This block is deliberately outside the ten sector ceilings. Government spending is partly financed by domestic borrowing, and banks hold and trade the securities through which that borrowing is raised. The interest on that debt is paid from public debt related costs, which is a first charge outside the sector ceilings, so this is a channel from the budget as a whole and not from any one sector line.

excluded.reason: Kenya Power recovers its revenue through electricity tariffs approved by the regulator, not through an allocation. The EII ceiling funds infrastructure in the sector it operates in, but a budget line is not a revenue line for it.
KenGen sells power under power purchase agreements. The EII ceiling funds capacity additions and drilling, but KenGen's revenue is contracted capacity and energy payments, not an allocation.
Kenya Pipeline earns transport tariffs on petroleum. Building it into a budget exposure would confuse a state owned transporter's tariff revenue with a budget line.
Umeme distributes electricity in Uganda. Kenya's budget does not fund the sector it operates in.

East African Breweries sells beer and spirits. No line in any of the ten sector ceilings buys brewing output, and there is no mechanical channel from education, health or security spending to its revenue.
British American Tobacco sells tobacco products. None of the ten ceilings buys them.

Safaricom sells connectivity mostly to retail and enterprise customers. It supplies government, but the sale is procurement spread across many votes and no single sector ceiling can be shown to carry it.
Absa NewGold ETF tracks the gold price. It has no revenue relationship with any budget line.
The Nairobi Securities Exchange earns listing, trading and data fees. A larger government budget does not mechanically pay it.

notes: A company can appear under more than one sector only where the money is different money. Cement appears under EII for roads and housing and under EPWNR for dams and water works, because those are two separate ceilings paying for two separate sets of works.

The map is deliberately thin. Most NSE listed companies have households or private firms as their customers, and the government is not their customer. Filling empty sectors with weak names would make the map look complete and would be wrong.
No entry states or implies a financial gain for any company, a movement in any share price, or that any security is a purchase or disposal candidate.
